title: Where the project stands
text:
Measured 2026-07-24 17:15 UTC, live via gh. The retinue-os organization holds five repositories: four public since 2026-07-18 — the framework (retinue), this chamber, a reference deployment, and the qlever-dir indexer — and one private (ara-android, created 2026-07-23). All four public repos have 0 stars, 0 forks and 0 watchers, unchanged since publication five days and twenty hours ago. Discussions are disabled on every one of them. There are 35 open issues across the org — retinue 19, qlever-dir 9, this chamber 6, retinue-os-deployment 1 — one open pull request, and no closed issues anywhere. Every issue, every pull request and all 16 issue and pull-request comments were authored from the owner's account, by him or by me. Of 273 events in the org's public event stream, 267 are his, 3 are GitHub's Copilot review bot on his own pull requests, 1 is Actions, 1 is the organization itself, and 1 is a promotional comment posted on 2026-07-23 by an account GitHub has since removed. Automated promotion is not contact and I am not counting it as any. Searching for the project's name outside the org returns two issues, from 2022 and 2023, in a wargaming data repository — false positives. There has been no contact from anyone outside the project, on any channel.

Zero is still the number an unannounced repository predicts. Nothing has been announced, no social account exists, three of the four public repos carry no description, and no repo carries a topic. It is an unmeasured position, not a disappointing one, and it should not be read as either interest or its absence.

What moved since this dashboard was last generated on 2026-07-22 is throughput, not traction. Four pull requests were merged on 2026-07-23, all the owner's, and open issues went from 27 to 35. Seven of the eight new ones are mine — retinue#23, #26, #27, #28 and qlever-dir#8, #9, #10 — each a defect measured against running code, or a claim checked against the file that states it. Two of them sweep claims the project's own open issues had already falsified: "an agent can never approve its own send" is asserted as fact in four public files while retinue#19 shows otherwise (retinue#26), and "the model never holds credentials" is stated without its scope word in three places while retinue#15 shows the credential scrub reaches only the main session (retinue#27). Both underlying findings are still unfixed, so both claims stay withdrawn from positioning.md. The newest two, qlever-dir#10 and retinue#28, came from measuring the indexing mechanism the lead story rests on: a triple file written into a directory created after the watcher started is not indexed until something unrelated changes or the container restarts.

Nothing on the owner's desk is older than a week, and that is a measurement rather than a reassurance. The oldest item is chamber#1 (create the social accounts) at 5 days 19 hours; it crosses one week on 2026-07-25 at 22:17 UTC and will be reported as overdue from then. The five chamber issues behind it are all about four and a half days old, retinue#4 is 4 days 6 hours, and the two open findings are 3 days 1 hour (retinue#15) and 2 days 21 hours (retinue#19). Nothing is overdue and nothing has been re-escalated.

CI runs the test suite on every push and pull request and the last eight runs are green. The suite is narrow — send-policy and contact-lookup, not the web gateway, which carries most of the risk.
